brief.title: Driver dispatch & proof-of-delivery platform
business_goals: Automate rider dispatch to improve efficiency.
Reduce 'item not received' disputes and associated chargebacks.
Improve visibility and control over rider movements.
Ensure real-time order status synchronization with Unicommerce.
Maintain dispatch performance during peak delivery volumes.

stakeholders.name: Karan Malhotra
concerns: Spike in 'item not received' disputes and chargebacks

stakeholders.name: Neha Iyer
concerns: Auto-assignment logic considering distance and rider load
Scope of route optimization (single-order assignment only for now)

stakeholders.name: Ravi Kumar
concerns: Rider mobile app with offline capability for patchy networks
Failed delivery reason codes and automatic reattempt triggers
App performance on low-end Android devices

stakeholders.name: Sameer Qureshi
concerns: Customer-facing live tracking update frequency (every 30 seconds)
Leveraging existing Google Maps Platform contract
Dispatch engine performance at peak (assign within 10 seconds for 9,000 deliveries/day)

constraints: Must integrate with existing order management system, Unicommerce; Unicommerce will not be replaced.
Must be live before the next big sale event (approximately ten weeks out).
Budget capped at 35 lakh for build plus first year of maps API costs.
Maps and routing must use the existing Google Maps Platform contract.
Rider mobile app must work with patchy network and queue updates offline.
Rider mobile app must run acceptably on low-end Android devices (contract workers' own phones).
Dispatch engine must assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order coming in, even at peak (9,000 deliveries/day).
Customer-facing tracking link needs to update rider's location at least every 30 seconds.
out_of_scope: Route optimization across an entire hub's deliveries — like solving the best order to visit 40 stops — is out of scope for this phase. We're doing single-order assignment only for now, batch routing is a phase two thing.
open_questions: What are the specific criteria for when a signature is required versus an OTP for proof of delivery?
How should failed delivery re-attempts be scheduled and managed by the system?
What are the minimum specifications for 'low-end Android' devices the app must support?
What are the requirements for the proof-of-delivery photo (e.g., timestamp, geotagging, resolution, storage)?

requirements.statement: The system shall auto-assign the nearest available rider to each order.
requirements.evidence: we need the system to auto-assign the nearest available rider to each order.

requirements.statement: The system shall consider both rider distance and current rider load when auto-assigning orders.
requirements.evidence: The auto-assignment needs to consider both distance and current rider load

requirements.statement: The system shall provide a mobile application for riders that displays their daily route.
requirements.evidence: Riders need a mobile app that shows their route for the day

requirements.statement: The rider mobile application shall queue updates offline and synchronize them when network connectivity is restored.
requirements.evidence: The app should queue updates offline and sync when signal comes back.

requirements.statement: The system shall require a photo and either a customer signature or a customer-entered OTP as proof of delivery before an order can be marked complete.
requirements.rationale: We had a spike in "item not received" disputes last quarter and it cost us badly on chargebacks.
requirements.evidence: every delivery needs a photo and either a signature or an OTP entered by the customer before it's marked complete.

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically send an OTP to the customer via SMS when the assigned rider is within 500 meters of the delivery location.
requirements.evidence: Ideally the OTP should be sent to the customer automatically via SMS when the rider is within, say, 500 meters of the drop location.
assumptions: The system can determine the rider's current location.
The system can determine the delivery location.
The system has access to customer phone numbers for SMS.

requirements.statement: The system shall update the rider's location on the customer-facing tracking link at least every 30 seconds.
requirements.evidence: the customer-facing tracking link needs to update the rider's location at least every 30 seconds.

requirements.statement: The system shall allow riders to select a reason code for failed deliveries.
requirements.evidence: Failed deliveries need a reason code — customer not available, wrong address, refused

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically schedule a reattempt for failed deliveries on the next day, for up to two total attempts, before marking the order for return to the hub.
requirements.evidence: those should automatically trigger a reattempt the next day, up to two attempts before we return it to the hub.

requirements.statement: The system shall integrate with Unicommerce to synchronize order status updates in real time.
requirements.evidence: We also need this to integrate with our existing order management system, Unicommerce, so that order status updates flow back there in real time.

requirements.statement: The dispatch engine shall assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order being received, even when processing 9,000 deliveries per day.
requirements.evidence: The dispatch engine has to assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order coming in, even at that peak.

requirements.statement: The system shall alert operations personnel when a rider deviates significantly from their assigned route.
requirements.evidence: Last month we had a rider go completely off-route for two hours and nobody noticed until the customer called to complain, that shouldn't be able to happen again.
assumptions: The system can define and track assigned routes.
The system can detect significant deviations from a route.

epics.title: Automated Dispatch & Assignment
epics.goal: To efficiently assign riders to orders based on proximity and load, ensuring quick dispatch times.

epics.title: Rider Delivery Workflow
epics.goal: To provide riders with the tools to manage their deliveries, capture proof of delivery, and handle failed attempts.

epics.title: Real-time Tracking & Visibility
epics.goal: To offer real-time tracking for customers and operational oversight for management, enhancing transparency and control.

epics.title: System Integrations
epics.goal: To ensure seamless, real-time synchronization of order statuses with external systems like Unicommerce.

stories.title: Synchronize order status with Unicommerce in real time

stories.so_that: Unicommerce always has the most current order information

acceptance_criteria.given: an order status changes (e.g., 'assigned', 'out for delivery', 'delivered') in our system

acceptance_criteria.then: the new status is immediately pushed to Unicommerce

issues: This story is a duplicate of S-006.
reviews.fix_instructions: Remove this story as it is identical to S-006.

issues: The story's interpretation of 'up to two total attempts' in R-009 (initial attempt + two reattempts, for a total of three attempts) deviates from the common understanding of 'up to two total attempts' (which typically means one initial attempt and one reattempt, for a total of two attempts). This adds scope beyond the requirement.
reviews.fix_instructions: Clarify with the product owner whether 'up to two total attempts' means one initial attempt plus one reattempt (total 2 attempts) or one initial attempt plus two reattempts (total 3 attempts). Adjust AC2 and AC3 to match the clarified requirement.

gaps.description: The system handles sensitive customer data (OTP, location) and proof-of-delivery photos. There are no explicit security requirements regarding data encryption, access control, or protection against unauthorized access/breaches.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the specific security requirements for protecting customer personal data, location tracking information, and proof-of-delivery records, including data at rest and in transit?

gaps.description: The system will generate significant data, including proof-of-delivery photos, signatures, OTP logs, rider location history, and failed delivery reasons. There are no requirements specifying data retention policies or storage capacity needs.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the data retention policies for proof-of-delivery photos, customer OTPs, rider location history, and other operational data generated by the system, and what are the associated storage requirements?

gaps.description: The constraint states the rider app must run 'acceptably' on low-end Android devices, but 'acceptably' is subjective and lacks measurable criteria.
related_ids: Constraint: Rider mobile app must run acceptably on low-end Android devices (contract workers' own phones).
gaps.suggested_question: What are the minimum performance benchmarks or specific device models that define 'acceptably' for the rider mobile app on low-end Android devices?

gaps.description: Requirement R-005 states 'either a customer signature or a customer-entered OTP' is required for proof of delivery, but it does not specify the conditions under which one method is preferred or mandatory over the other.
gaps.suggested_question: Under what specific circumstances should a customer signature be required for proof of delivery, versus a customer-entered OTP?

gaps.description: Requirement R-008 states riders can select a reason code for failed deliveries, but the specific list of codes, who defines them, and their impact on the system (e.g., triggering specific workflows) are not defined.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the predefined reason codes for failed deliveries, and what actions or workflows should each code trigger within the system?

gaps.description: No Legal or Compliance stakeholder is mentioned, despite the system handling personal data and aiming to reduce disputes, which have legal implications.
gaps.suggested_question: Who is responsible for defining the legal and compliance requirements related to customer data privacy, data retention, and the handling of delivery disputes?

gaps.description: Customer Support will handle customer inquiries related to tracking, OTPs, and failed deliveries, but their specific needs for tools or information are not captured.
gaps.suggested_question: What information and tools will Customer Support need to effectively assist customers with tracking inquiries, OTP issues, and failed delivery resolutions?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog provides good coverage for the stated business goals and functional requirements, particularly around automating dispatch, proof of delivery, and real-time tracking. Key performance targets for dispatch and tracking are also addressed. However, there are significant ambiguities in core features like proof-of-delivery conditions and failed delivery reasons, which could lead to implementation challenges or operational inconsistencies. Additionally, critical non-functional aspects like data security and retention, along with the needs of key stakeholders like Legal/Compliance and Customer Support, are not explicitly covered, posing potential risks for compliance, system robustness, and operational efficiency.
